finding: Hotspawn lists WROTBERRY where current external schedules use WBT. This is now mapped for Elisa BreakOut Series #2 only, on fixture parity rather than a name guess: Hotspawn's WROTBERRY occupies the same group slot as HLTV's and Polymarket's WBT against the same opponents (EAC, ENCE, BOJONG) with matching UTC starts, and only one team can occupy that slot in a four-team group. WhiteBIT's white.market announcement launches WhiteBIT Team (WBT) with the Ukrainian core that third-party databases recorded under the WROTBERRY tag. No official statement was found that says 'WROTBERRY was renamed WBT', so the mapping stays visible here for manual review; odds are transferred only for a fixture whose opponent pair and UTC start match exactly.

Some exchange markets have quoted prices but fail the project's spread/liquidity policy. A visible midpoint is not reliable evidence of a precise win chance. Rejected observations and their exact raw inputs are retained in the evidence ledger, not presented as actionable picks. A later six-hour refresh may find a usable line.

finding: The official scheduled feed retains past-start and past-lock records, sometimes with an end time. All returned CS2 entries remain visible, but these rows are not treated as upcoming picks or asserted to be completed results. Missing series format is left blank. A page/API field conflict blocks that row's recommendation.

HLTV was checked first for missing picks; retrieved match pages exposed context but not a verified numeric bookmaker pair. Pinnacle supplied usable fallback moneylines. Thunderpick and Rivalry returned application shells to the runner, Stake returned HTTP 403, and GG.BET restricted access. A separately rendered Thunderpick page did show prices, but did not establish a repeatable validated UTC/quote adapter for this collector. HTTP 200 alone is not accepted as successful odds collection. No access restrictions are bypassed.

These are our calculated, margin-removed market lines, not a calibrated independent performance model or multi-book consensus. HLTV rankings, historical win rates, Valve points and fan votes are not converted into invented percentages. Team-organization aliases are narrowly sourced; they do not certify the current player roster. Missing information cannot justify a forced pick or a default 50/50.

The inherited audits found source-update expiry omission, acceptance of non-finite liquidity, incomplete raw-evidence validation, and possible inventory loss on a wrong-game response. These were independently reproduced and fixed. The preserved audit findings describe the historical baseline; current tests verify the corrected behavior. Live deployment is verified separately from a passing branch build.

Coverage decision: a fixture with no other usable line may now be priced from a two-sided exchange quote that fails only the 25-point spread ceiling, provided the market is open, accepting orders, has a fresh observation and update, and holds at least $100 of liquidity. The real spread and the strict rejection are published on the row and in the evidence ledger, the row is labelled low confidence, and a 60-point ceiling still applies. This raises coverage without inventing numbers, but a wide mid is a low-precision estimate and is not comparable in quality to a strict-tier line.

finding: Coverage decision: when no market line exists at all, a pick may be published from an exact HLTV fixture identity with both teams' world rankings, choosing the better-ranked side. No percentage or fair line is published for these rows and every one is labelled research-only, so a ranked comparison is never presented as a market probability. Rows without both verified ranks stay unresolved.

The day-1 review on the analysis page mixes source quality and says so per row: series scores and the 9z stats come from HLTV, the Aurora rebuild timeline from a roster report plus Hotspawn's own tracker, the fatigue read from a betting preview (commentary), and map-level detail for the Falcons-NIP game from that same preview. Hotspawn's pick'em scoring rules were not collected, so no points-weight claim is made.
